precepts.text: I take not this my sister for lust, but uprightly: therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together. We pray we see our older years together. Some of us make it there and some do not; let it be because of passing, not because you would not apply the scriptures. The prophecy classes are dope, but you have to have the same zeal for these classes on marriage and repentance, or your marriage falls apart and then you look at us like it was our fault.
precepts.point: Those of you married a long time are supposed to still be able to look at your wife or your husband and see when you were young. That is why people who have that can be content: as you get older, both of you change, both of you get old, but you remember. Let her breast satisfy thee at all times; and be thou ravished always with her love. Her body will change with the years, but she is yours, brother, and that bond cannot be broken if you are in the Lord.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
Marriage was designed to happen when you are young: you meet a young woman, and this is the person you grow old with. “rejoice with the wife of thy youth.” Tobias prayed the same thing on his wedding night: “And now, O Lord, I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly: therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.”

Hands went up around the room for five, ten, fifteen, twenty and twenty-five years of marriage and more, and the Bishop has been married 36 years. These are the examples we have right here. Those married a long time are supposed to still be able to look at their wife or husband and see when they were young. That is why they can be content: both of you change, both of you get old, but you remember.

“let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; and be thou ravished always with her love.” When you marry her young her breasts are at three o'clock; as you grow old together they will be at six. But they are yours, brother, no matter what time it is. You walk in the room and she is the only thing you see. That bond can't be broken if you are in the Lord.

So we pray we are able to see our older years together. Some of us make it there and some don't; let it be because of passing, not because you weren't applying the scriptures or listening in class. The prophecy classes are dope, but you have to have the same zeal for the classes on marriage and repentance and apply them in your everyday life. Otherwise your marriage falls apart, your kids go who knows where, and then you look at us like it was our fault.

precepts.text: Let thy fountain be blessed, and rejoice with the wife of thy youth; let her be as the loving hind and pleasant roe, let her breasts satisfy thee at all times, and be thou ravished always with her love. Passion after the foundation, and it cannot exist if the divine parts of the marriage are not set up correctly.
precepts.point: He took her uprightly and they aged together mercifully, and with age comes beauty, love, and passion, not whimsical movie feelings. Stop chasing a feeling; get your mind like Tobit's. If even a majority of families moved in that spirit, how much stronger are we as a people for the time of trouble to come. Weddings are not done here for anyone who has not proved for three years.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
You want passion in the relationship? Here it is: “Let thy fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of thy youth. Let her be as the loving hind and pleasant roe; let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; and be thou ravished always with her love.”

Ravished is not a regular word: it means to fill someone with intense delight and rapture. Delight, charm, enthral, captivate, spellbind, bewitch, fascinate. That goes into the power a woman has in her voice and her conversation. There's your passion, there's your romance, after the foundation of your marriage is set up correctly and you age together.

But that can't exist if the other, divine parts of the marriage are not set up correctly; it's not going to happen. You don't seek this first. It's like looking for furniture, things for the walls, carpet and rugs, when you haven't even bought the house yet and don't know if the walls will hold or the foundation is strong. That's how we treat marriage nowadays.

Tobias did it in the right order: “I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly”. The being ravished always with her love comes after that foundation, as the fruit of it.

precepts.text: The lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, but her end is bitter as wormwood; her ways are moveable.
precepts.point: The scriptures warn of that spirit: the woman whose heart is snares and nets and her hands as bands; whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her. The lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, but her end is bitter, and her ways are moveable; the same mouth that flattered turns and accuses.

note.label: Genesis 39: Joseph in Potiphar's House

precepts.why:
“For the lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, and her mouth is smoother than oil: But her end is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a twoedged sword.” The lips that said “Lie with me” day by day were smooth as oil; the end of it was bitter as wormwood. “Her feet go down to death; her steps take hold on hell.”

“her ways are moveable, that thou canst not know them.” The same mouth that flattered Joseph turned and accused him: “The Hebrew servant, which thou hast brought unto us, came in unto me to mock me.” She moved from wanting him to destroying him, holding his garment as proof. That is what a strange woman is, and that is why Joseph was right to flee her.

precepts.text: The priest's lips keep knowledge, so knowledge is tied to the law and the commandments.
precepts.point: Attend to wisdom and bow your ear to understanding so that you may regard knowledge. The knowledge spoken of here is the commandments of the Most High.

note.label: Proverbs 5: The Strange Woman and Thy Labours in the House of a Stranger

precepts.why:
“My son, attend unto my wisdom, and bow thine ear to my understanding: That thou mayest regard discretion, and that thy lips may keep knowledge.” The knowledge spoken of here is the commandments of the Most High.

Malachi shows that: “For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.” The priest's lips keep knowledge, and what is sought at his mouth is the law. Knowledge is tied to the law and the commandments.

So lips that keep knowledge are lips that keep the law. Attend to wisdom and bow your ear to understanding so that you may regard knowledge, which is the commandments.

precepts.text: Do not give what is holy to the dogs nor cast your pearls before swine; the pearls are the word of the Most High, not to be handed to strangers.
precepts.point: Giving your honour to others is like giving what is holy to strangers. Too often our people care more about the other nations repenting and getting into the kingdom than about our own repentance, and want the other nations ruling with us in the kingdom.

note.label: Proverbs 5: The Strange Woman and Thy Labours in the House of a Stranger

precepts.why:
“Remove thy way far from her, and come not nigh the door of her house: Lest thou give thine honour unto others, and thy years unto the cruel”. Giving your honour to others is like giving what is holy to strangers.

Christ says: “Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.” The pearls are the word of the Most High, not to be handed to strangers. Hand it to the dogs and the swine and they trample it and turn and rend you.

Too often our people care more about the other nations repenting and getting into the kingdom than about our own repentance, and want the other nations ruling with us in the kingdom. That is giving your honour to others and your years to the cruel. Remove your way far from her.

precepts.text: Tyre and Zidon and the coasts of Palestine took the Most High's silver and gold and carried His goodly pleasant things into their temples.
precepts.point: We are living this now. Every time a foreign king came up to invade Israel he stripped the silver and gold and pleasant things out of the temple and exacted tribute. In this captivity Esau still profits off our labour and our inventions, the light filament, the plasma and open heart surgery, the cotton gin, computers and cell phones, yet makes no account of who produced them.

note.label: Proverbs 5: The Strange Woman and Thy Labours in the House of a Stranger

precepts.why:
“Lest strangers be filled with thy wealth; and thy labours be in the house of a stranger”. Your labours are the riches that come from your work ending up in the house of strangers.

Joel shows it happening: “Yea, and what have ye to do with me, O Tyre, and Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine? will ye render me a recompence? and if ye recompense me, swiftly and speedily will I return your recompence upon your own head; Because ye have taken my silver and my gold, and have carried into your temples my goodly pleasant things”. Tyre and Zidon and the coasts of Palestine took the Most High's silver and gold and carried his goodly pleasant things into their temples. Every time a foreign king came up to invade Israel he stripped the silver and gold and pleasant things out of the temple and exacted tribute.

We are living this now. In this captivity Esau still profits off our labour and our inventions, the light filament, the plasma and open heart surgery, the cotton gin, computers and cell phones, yet makes no account of who produced them. Strangers are filled with our wealth, and the Most High promises to return their recompence on their own head.

precepts.text: Esau is condemned for entering the gate of the Most High's people in their calamity and laying hands on their substance.
precepts.point: We are living this now. Every time a foreign king came up to invade Israel he stripped the silver and gold and pleasant things out of the temple and exacted tribute. In this captivity Esau still profits off our labour and our inventions, the light filament, the plasma and open heart surgery, the cotton gin, computers and cell phones, yet makes no account of who produced them.

note.label: Proverbs 5: The Strange Woman and Thy Labours in the House of a Stranger

precepts.why:
“Lest strangers be filled with thy wealth; and thy labours be in the house of a stranger”. Obadiah names the stranger who did it: Esau. “But thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction; neither shouldest thou have spoken proudly in the day of distress. Thou shouldest not have entered into the gate of my people in the day of their calamity; yea, thou shouldest not have looked on their affliction in the day of their calamity, nor have laid hands on their substance in the day of their calamity”.

Esau is condemned for entering the gate of the Most High's people in their calamity and laying hands on their substance. That substance is our labours in the house of a stranger.

We are living this now. In this captivity Esau still profits off our labour and our inventions, the light filament, the plasma and open heart surgery, the cotton gin, computers and cell phones, yet makes no account of who produced them. He laid hands on our substance in the day of our calamity, just as Obadiah says.

precepts.text: Laban confesses he has learned by experience that the Most High blessed him for Jacob's sake, as the nations are blessed for Israel's sake today.
precepts.point: We are living this now. Every time a foreign king came up to invade Israel he stripped the silver and gold and pleasant things out of the temple and exacted tribute. In this captivity Esau still profits off our labour and our inventions, the light filament, the plasma and open heart surgery, the cotton gin, computers and cell phones, yet makes no account of who produced them.

note.label: Proverbs 5: The Strange Woman and Thy Labours in the House of a Stranger

precepts.why:
“Lest strangers be filled with thy wealth; and thy labours be in the house of a stranger”. Jacob's labours were in the house of Laban, and Laban knew what he was getting from it: “And Laban said unto him, I pray thee, if I have found favour in thine eyes, tarry: for I have learned by experience that the Lord hath blessed me for thy sake.”

Laban confesses he has learned by experience that the Most High blessed him for Jacob's sake. The stranger was filled with wealth because Israel was laboring in his house.

That is how the nations are blessed for Israel's sake today. Esau profits off our labour and our inventions in this captivity and makes no account of who produced them, but like Laban, the blessing came for Jacob's sake.

precepts.text: You have set at nought all counsel and would have none of reproof, matching the man who hated instruction.
precepts.point: Drink waters out of your own cistern and running waters out of your own well. This is a call to stay with your own people and your own nationality.

note.label: Proverbs 5: The Strange Woman and Thy Labours in the House of a Stranger

precepts.why:
The man who despised instruction mourns at the last: “How have I hated instruction, and my heart despised reproof; And have not obeyed the voice of my teachers, nor inclined mine ear to them that instructed me!” The commandments and the prophets are the teachers meant here.

Wisdom said it of him already in Proverbs 1: “But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof”. Setting counsel at nought and refusing reproof is the very thing he confesses too late: he hated instruction and despised reproof.

He ends up almost in all evil in the midst of the congregation and assembly. The one who would have none of reproof is the one who mourns at the last.

precepts.text: Isaac was seen sporting with Rebekah his wife, the picture of a husband playing lovingly with his own wife.
precepts.point: Be ravished always with her love, not with another woman. Married love within your own nation is what is blessed here.

note.label: Proverbs 5: The Strange Woman and Thy Labours in the House of a Stranger

precepts.why:
“Let thy fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of thy youth. Let her be as the loving hind and pleasant roe; let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; and be thou ravished always with her love.” Be ravished always with her love, not with another woman.

Isaac is the picture of it: “And it came to pass, when he had been there a long time, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a window, and saw, and, behold, Isaac was sporting with Rebekah his wife.” Isaac was seen sporting with Rebekah his wife, a husband playing lovingly with his own wife.

That is the fountain that is your own and not strangers' with you. Married love within your own nation is what is blessed here.

precepts.text: The jews had married wives of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab, and even Solomon was caused to sin by outlandish women; strange wives are women of the other nations.
precepts.point: The ways of a man are before the eyes of the Most High and He ponders all his goings. The wicked man's own iniquities take him and he is held with the cords of his sins, dying without instruction in the greatness of his folly.

note.label: Proverbs 5: The Strange Woman and Thy Labours in the House of a Stranger

precepts.why:
“And why wilt thou, my son, be ravished with a strange woman, and embrace the bosom of a stranger?” The strange woman carries a double meaning: a woman of another nation, and a woman outside of your own wife. Nehemiah shows the first.

“In those days also saw I Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab: And their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews’ language, but according to the language of each people.” The jews had married wives of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab, and their children could not even speak the language. Nehemiah “contended with them, and cursed them, and smote certain of them, and plucked off their hair, and made them swear by God, saying, Ye shall not give your daughters unto their sons, nor take their daughters unto your sons, or for yourselves.”

Then he brings Solomon himself: “Did not Solomon king of Israel sin by these things? yet among many nations was there no king like him, who was beloved of his God, and God made him king over all Israel: nevertheless even him did outlandish women cause to sin.” Even Solomon was caused to sin by outlandish women. Strange wives are women of the other nations, and the man who embraces the bosom of a stranger is held with the cords of his sins.

precepts.text: The sons of Israel confess marrying strange wives of the nations, so the strange woman is a woman of the other nations.
precepts.point: The ways of a man are before the eyes of the Most High and He ponders all his goings. The wicked man's own iniquities take him and he is held with the cords of his sins, dying without instruction in the greatness of his folly.

note.label: Proverbs 5: The Strange Woman and Thy Labours in the House of a Stranger

precepts.why:
“And why wilt thou, my son, be ravished with a strange woman, and embrace the bosom of a stranger?” The strange woman is a woman of another nation, and Israel confessed it as sin in the days of Esdras: “Then Jechonias the son of Jeelus, one of the sons of Israel, called out, and said, O Esdras, we have sinned against the Lord God, we have married strange women of the nations of the land, and now is all Israel aloft.”

The sons of Israel confess marrying strange wives of the nations of the land. Strange women are the women of the other nations, and marrying them was a sin against the Lord God.

That is the stranger whose bosom Solomon warns against. The strange woman carries a double meaning, a woman of another nation and a woman outside of your own wife, and here the first meaning is spelled out by Israel's own confession.

precepts.text: Jephthah is thrust out as the son of a strange woman, that strange woman being likened to an harlot.
precepts.point: The ways of a man are before the eyes of the Most High and He ponders all his goings. The wicked man's own iniquities take him and he is held with the cords of his sins, dying without instruction in the greatness of his folly.

note.label: Proverbs 5: The Strange Woman and Thy Labours in the House of a Stranger

precepts.why:
“And why wilt thou, my son, be ravished with a strange woman, and embrace the bosom of a stranger?” Jephthah shows what comes of it. “Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valour, and he was the son of an harlot: and Gilead begat Jephthah.” When Gilead's wife's sons grew up, “they thrust out Jephthah, and said unto him, Thou shalt not inherit in our father’s house; for thou art the son of a strange woman.”

Jephthah is thrust out as the son of a strange woman, and that strange woman is likened to an harlot. The strange woman carries a double meaning, a woman of another nation and a woman outside of your own wife, and Jephthah's mother was that harlot outside the wife.

The son of the strange woman lost his inheritance in his father's house. That is the cord of his father's sin holding the next generation.
